title: Social Proof

scenes.text: One sentence got more hotel guests to *reuse towels*.
scenes.vo: Changing one sentence on a card got more hotel guests to reuse their towels.
Researchers tested cards in hotel rooms. Card A asked guests to help save the environment.

scenes.text: Card B: “Most guests in this hotel reuse their towels”
scenes.vo: Card B simply said that most guests at this hotel reuse their towels.
Card B won. 44 percent reused towels, compared with 35 percent.
And when the card said most guests who stayed in this very room reused towels, it rose to 49 percent.

scenes.text:
*Social proof*:
we copy people like us
scenes.vo: This is social proof. When we're unsure what to do, we copy people like us.
It's why reviews, bestseller tags and 'two thousand people bought this' work so well.

scenes.text: Persuading someone? Show what others *already do*.
scenes.vo: So when you're persuading someone, don't just say why it's good. Show what others already do.

scenes.text:
Follow *@inquisitive_bytes*
for a daily byte of behaviour science
scenes.vo: Follow Inquisitive Bytes for a daily byte of behaviour science.

caption:
We don't just follow the crowd, we follow the crowd most like us. 🏨

What's the last thing you bought because 'everyone' had it? 👇
source: Goldstein, N. J., Cialdini, R. B. & Griskevicius, V. (2008). A Room with a Viewpoint. Journal of Consumer Research, 35(3).
